naming_collision.one_line_test: If it is about WHO the user is, it is Track A. If it is about WHERE the UI shows up, it is Track B.
naming_collision.how_they_fit_together: HXL renders an agent's UI on any surface but does not answer who is asking. The default agent integration runs as an integration user - one credential with broad visibility, where the agent decides what to reveal, which is the design security teams reject. Track A supplies a named-user token instead, so the widget shows one specific customer's data with Salesforce sharing enforcing it. Neither track can make that claim alone.

executive_summary.what_it_is: A working demo of Salesforce Headless Identity: a custom front end with Salesforce behind it and no Salesforce UI anywhere. Users authenticate and read their own records without ever seeing a Salesforce-hosted page or a *.force.com redirect.
executive_summary.the_argument: Salesforce keeps identity, sharing and data. You keep the entire experience. The UI does not have to look like, or be built with, Salesforce.
executive_summary.architecture: browser -> (HttpOnly session cookie) -> Node BFF (this repo, holds client secret + tokens) -> (OAuth + Bearer) -> Salesforce Experience Cloud site + Apex REST
executive_summary.why_a_BFF: The browser never receives a client id, a client secret or an access token - only an opaque session cookie. That is the difference between a headless *layer* and shipping OAuth into a browser.
executive_summary.current_completion: Roughly 60% of the intended demo. The core architectural argument is provable today; three of four identity flows are blocked on org configuration, not on code.

findings.title: developer.salesforce.com 403s automated fetch
findings.detail: The entire HXL developer guide is unreachable to any scripted client - the same wall Track A hit. Everything was reconstructed from a public example repo plus the org's own error messages. Budget for reading the docs by hand in a browser.

findings.title: The platform validates Mosaic JSON server-side, strictly, and the errors are excellent
findings.detail: A deploy is not a rubber stamp. Two rules that cost a deploy cycle: tile/card caps at 10 children ('The block tile/card at the path $.widgetBody.children[0].children[0] can have only 10 children'), and tile/column does not accept padding, only gap ('You can't add the padding property ... because the additionalProperties keyword value is set to false'). Errors name the exact JSON path, which makes this pleasant to debug - unlike Track A's identity wall, where everything failed with 'authentication failure'.

findings.title: The public example's JSON would not deploy as-is
findings.detail: The widget in Lakshmikanth-Paruchuru/hxl-agentic-experience-layer puts padding on a tile/column and 13 children in a tile/card. It was written against API 65; this org is 67. Treat any HXL example older than your org's API version as a sketch, not a spec.

findings.title: Claude Desktop needs native stdio and absolute paths
findings.detail: No CDN, no mcp-remote, no relative paths. The widget iframe is sandboxed without network access, so the ext-apps runtime is read off disk and inlined into the HTML at server start. A <script src> to a CDN fails silently - a blank card and no error.

findings.title: UiWidgetBundle and McpServerDefinition were both already available
findings.detail: Present as deployable metadata types in a plain Developer Edition org at API 67, with no special enablement request. Nothing had ever been deployed with them before this project - hxlOrderCard is the first.

findings.title: Returning null from an Apex REST method on 404 yields a non-JSON body
findings.detail: The BFF read it as "answered with HTML, not JSON". Return an empty DTO with the status code instead.

findings.title: One identity per process is a leak the moment the server is hosted
findings.detail: Over stdio, HXL_DEMO_USER is one laptop's customer. Over a public URL it is every host user seeing Ada. Hence per-session sign_in and env identity off on HTTP by default.

identity_flows.common_shape: Every flow ends at the same place: an authorization code exchanged with grant_type=authorization_code. Only how the code is obtained varies. Authorize is always POST <site>/services/oauth2/authorize with response_type=code_credentials.
identity_flows.host_rule: Identity calls go to the Experience Cloud site domain, never to login.salesforce.com. Data calls are the opposite: the site 302-redirects /services/apexrest/* to its own login page, so those go to the instance_url that came back with the token. hxl.js handles the split via apiHost().

flows.notes: One round trip. PKCE S256 applied.

flows.authorize_headers: Auth-Request-Type: user-registration, Auth-Verification-Type: email + Basic base64(identifier:otp)
flows.notes: Creates the user and signs them in.

flows.authorize_headers: Auth-Request-Type: passwordless-login, Auth-Verification-Type: email + Basic base64(identifier:otp)
flows.notes: No password anywhere in the exchange.
Same endpoint twice: request OTP, then reset with otp + newpassword. Produces no session.

identity_flows.response_quirk: A successful headless authorize can answer 302 with the code in the Location header rather than as JSON. That is the happy path, not a bounce. hxl.js call() takes {redirectOk} and authorize() opts in, reading the code from Location, then res.code, then res.redirect_uri - three shapes across releases.
identity_flows.init_handle_quirk: The init endpoints' handle is read as `identifier` with a fallback to `request_id`; Salesforce has used both names across releases.

org_divergences.title: PKCE is forced on and cannot be disabled
org_divergences.detail: The External Client App shows 'Require Proof Key for Code Exchange' greyed out - 'contact Support' to change it. hxl.js implements PKCE S256: a 64-byte base64url verifier, code_challenge + code_challenge_method=S256 on authorize, code_verifier on exchange. Both params are conditional, so the code still runs against an org where PKCE is off.

org_divergences.title: It is an External Client App, not a classic connected app
org_divergences.detail: Different UI and different metadata. Drive it from the CLI instead of fighting the form. AllSelfAuthorized DOES NOT WORK for Experience Cloud users - it returns 'invalid_app_access: user is not admin approved to access this app'. You must use AdminApprovedPreAuthorized AND add the 'HXL customer' profile to the app's approved profiles. This was the single blocker on the login flow. Warning: editing policies in the UI overwrites whatever the CLI last deployed, including fields you did not touch.

org_divergences.title: Authorize answers with a 302, not JSON
org_divergences.detail: A successful headless authorize returns HTTP 302 with the code in the Location header. The original hxl.js treated every 3xx as a bounce to a hosted login page and threw. call() now takes {redirectOk}; other 3xx still error, and that check is still worth having.

org_divergences.title: Apex REST must go to instance_url, not the site host
org_divergences.detail: The site 302-redirects /services/apexrest/* to its login page. getMyOrders, createOrder and userinfo now take the instance_url that came back with the token; server.js passes s.tokens.instance_url through. Identity still happens on the site host - only the data calls move.

org_divergences.title: Community users need ApiEnabled
org_divergences.detail: Without it Apex REST returns APEX_REST_SERVICES_DISABLED. Added to HXL_Customer_Access as a userPermissions entry. UNRESOLVED LICENSING CAVEAT: ada.hxl is a Customer Community (CSP_LITE_PORTAL) user, a licence that does not normally include API access, yet the grant deployed and works. Confirm this is legitimate before relying on it - Customer Community Plus is the licence that formally includes API access.

org_divergences.title: Required fields cannot appear in fieldPermissions
org_divergences.detail: The deploy failed with 'You cannot deploy to a required field: HXL_Order__c.Status__c'. Status__c is required, so the platform grants it implicitly. That block was removed from the permission set; no access is lost.

org_divergences.title: The role assignment silently did not save
org_divergences.detail: SETUP.md step 4 is right that the admin needs a role, but the UI reported success without persisting it. Verify with SOQL, do not trust the screen: sf data query --query "SELECT Name, UserRole.Name FROM User WHERE Username='...'" and fix with sf data update record --sobject User --where "Username='...'" --values "UserRoleId=00Eg8000005clflEAA"

org_divergences.title: HXL_OrderAPITest needs Digital Experiences before it will pass
org_divergences.detail: makePortalUser guards only against NO portal profile existing. This org has one, so the guard passes and 'insert u' then fails, demanding Setup > Digital Experiences > Settings > 'Allow using standard external profiles for self-registration, user creation, and login'. That checkbox is NOT in SETUP.md step 6. Deploy with -SkipTests until it is ticked.

org_divergences.title: verify-setup.ps1 had a false-negative bug (fixed)
org_divergences.detail: Invoke-Soql did 'return @($res.records)'. PowerShell unrolls a single-element array back to a bare object, and PSCustomObject has no .Count in PS 5.1 - so EVERY check that matched exactly one record reported failure. It claimed the permission set, role and account were all missing when all three existed. Fixed with 'return ,@(...)'. It still warns 'No connected apps visible'; that is a false alarm - ConnectedApplication is not reliably queryable and this org uses an External Client App anyway.

org_divergences.title: "View All" on the customer profile was silently defeating the sharing claim (found and fixed 2026-09-12)
org_divergences.detail: The HXL customer profile had PermissionsViewAllRecords=true on HXL_Order__c, which bypasses OWD and sharing. Every earlier "sharing proof" was the WHERE Owner_Contact__c filter in getMyOrders. The new get_order tool (by Id, no filter) returned Grace Hopper's $9,999 order to Ada on first run. Fix, in source and deployed: profiles/HXL customer.profile-meta.xml (viewAllRecords=false, allowEdit=true) + sharingSets/HXL_Customer_Orders (Edit on orders whose Owner_Contact__c is the user's Contact). Re-verified: Grace's order found:false by number and Id; Ada's 16 orders unchanged incl. 3 admin-created ones now visible via the sharing set. Check every community profile/permset: PermissionsViewAllRecords and PermissionsModifyAllRecords must both be false.

org_divergences.title: WITH USER_MODE + missing FLS reports as "Variable does not exist: tmpVar1"
org_divergences.detail: Hit in HXL_OrderAPITest when the portal test user lacked FLS on the new Channel__c field. Fix: assign HXL_Customer_Access to the test user inside System.runAs(current user) to avoid MIXED_DML_OPERATION, and prefer the real "HXL customer" profile so the sharing set applies in tests.

init_endpoint_wall.summary: Login & Registration refuses to enable Headless Registration, Passwordless Login or Forgot Password unless each has 'Require authentication' OR 'Require reCAPTCHA' ticked. This is enforced, not advisory - the Metadata API rejects it too. With Require authentication on, the init endpoints reject every credential that can be minted.

first_party_route.what: OAuth 2.0 for First-Party Applications - the newer protocol that replaces the init endpoints, and almost certainly the intended path in this release.
first_party_route.enabled_in_org: YES - both flags were needed: isFirstPartyAppsAllowed on the Network metadata (site) and isFirstPartyAppEnabled on ExtlClntAppOauthSettings (the app). Enabling only the site flag gives 'first party applications not enabled for application'.
first_party_route.endpoint: POST <site>/services/oauth2/v1/authorization_challenge (the unversioned path also answers; /services/oauth2/challenge is a 404)
first_party_route.body_takes: username, password, client_id, code_challenge, and client_assertion - 'the client attestation JWT that you generated, signed by the certificate'
first_party_route.blocker: Every request without a valid client_assertion returns {"error_description":"invalid assertion","error_code":"invalid_grant","error":"invalid_request"}. A dummy value returns the identical error, confirming it is required and verified. auth_request_type, client_secret and the Auth-Request-Type header make no difference - the assertion check happens first.
first_party_route.to_unblock: Generate a signing certificate, register it on the External Client App for client attestation, then have the BFF mint and sign a JWT per request. Real work, but well-defined - unlike the init-endpoint dead end.

A Google reCAPTCHA key and a real solve in the browser

init_endpoint_wall.recommendation: The first-party route: it is the direction Salesforce is moving, it needs no captcha in the demo, and the failure mode is now fully understood.

gotchas: THE UI FORM SILENTLY FAILS TO SAVE. The role, selfRegistration and the registration auth flag all looked saved and were not. Always confirm against metadata or SOQL, never against the screen.

Two OAuth flags, not one: 'Allow Authorization Code and Credentials Flows' exists org-wide (Setup > OAuth and OpenID Connect Settings) AND on the connected app. Both must be on, or you get a redirect to a hosted login page instead of JSON.
The admin user needs a role. Self-registration creates portal users under a business Account and Salesforce refuses when the account owner has no role. The error does not mention roles.
The permission set must reach the SITE's profile, not just you. A perfectly valid token otherwise gets a 403 from Apex.
SF_REDIRECT_URI must match the registered callback byte for byte, trailing slash included.
The authorization code is single-use and short-lived. invalid_grant on the token exchange usually means a replay or clock skew.
OTP email never arriving is usually Deliverability set to 'System email only'. Setup > Deliverability > Access level: All email.
An empty orders list with a null contactId means the token belongs to a user with no Contact - an internal user, not a community user.

OBSERVATION, NOT YET VERIFIED: scripts/seed-demo-data.apex has DEMO_EMAIL = 'ada@example.com', while the working test user is ada.hxl@hxlpoc.demo. If seeded orders do not appear for the logged-in user, this mismatch is the first thing to check.
View All / Modify All on any community profile or permset silently defeats sharing. A filtered query proves nothing about the platform - only an unfiltered ask that is refused does.
On Windows, Start-Process npm starts nothing (npm is a .cmd shim). Use node app/server.js / node mcp/server-http.mjs directly.
Free cloudflared tunnel URLs rotate on every restart - re-paste into ChatGPT/Slack.
The site's DNS blips on first contact; the MCP server retries once so the card does not show "sample data" for no visible reason.

decision_made.decision: Build Track B (Headless Experience Layer) from scratch, keep Track A intact, and wire them together rather than choosing between them. Taken with more than 10 of the 30 hours remaining.
decision_made.outcome: Spike succeeded. The widget bundle deployed to the org on the second attempt, the MCP server works, and live named-user data flows from Track A into the widget payload. The combined story - an agent surface showing one customer's data with Salesforce sharing enforcing it - is now demonstrable up to the host render.
decision_made.what_was_rejected: Scrapping Track A (its findings are the hardest-won material in the project), and pursuing the Track A certificate route in parallel (splitting time across two hard problems).

superseded_options.note: These were the differentiating ideas considered before Track B was chosen. Kept for the record; none were built.
superseded_options.context: The Track A demo alone proves the well-known claim - custom UI, Salesforce backend - which every Headless Identity demo proves. The options below were ways to differentiate it.

open_decision_superseded.context: SUPERSEDED by decision_made above - kept for the record. No code was written for any of these options; the Identity Broker insight was instead absorbed into the Track A + Track B bridge.
open_decision_superseded.the_insight: The genuinely differentiated asset in this repo is token custody in the layer. Because the BFF holds the token rather than the browser holding a force.com session cookie, capabilities become possible that Salesforce-hosted UI structurally cannot offer.

options.name: Identity Broker (recommended)
options.summary: The layer as a channel-agnostic session broker.
capabilities: Cross-device handoff via a short-lived pairing code - desktop to kiosk or phone, one Salesforce identity, no re-login.
Step-up re-authentication - a high-value order forces a fresh Salesforce credential check before the write, time-boxed and recorded.
Session inventory and revoke-everywhere across all channels.
options.why_it_wins: All three are impossible with Salesforce-hosted UI, and all three run on the login flow that already works - no dependency on the blocked init endpoints.
options.sketch: POST /api/pair -> 6-digit code, 90s TTL. POST /api/orders over a threshold -> 401 step_up_required -> fresh headless authorize -> write. GET/DELETE /api/sessions for the inventory and revocation.

options.name: Progressive identity
options.summary: An anonymous guest session carrying a cart, bound to a real Salesforce identity at the moment of conversion with zero state loss and no redirect.
options.caveat: The full version (guest to brand-new user) needs the registration flow, which is blocked. Only the bind-to-existing-user half is shippable today.

options.name: Non-browser channel
options.summary: Drive the same layer from a terminal or kiosk client and an SMS/chat-style client, proving Salesforce identity reaches surfaces that cannot render a hosted login page.
options.caveat: Very visual on stage, but thinner as an architecture argument.

Everything you saw is Salesforce identity, Salesforce sharing, Salesforce data. What you did not see is Salesforce UI. Swap this front end for React, Next, iOS, a kiosk, a set-top box - the layer does not change.

anticipated_questions.a: Yes. Headless Identity runs through an Experience Cloud site; the users are Customer Community (or Partner) users and are licensed as such. The site being invisible does not make it free.
There is a headless flow for that too - headless SSO with an external auth provider. Same shape, different init call. Not wired up here.

anticipated_questions.q: Why the BFF? Can't the SPA call Salesforce directly?
anticipated_questions.a: It can, as a public client with PKCE and reCAPTCHA. Then the tokens live in the browser and the init endpoints are internet-facing and unauthenticated. The BFF exists so neither is true.
The headless auth endpoints are subject to org API limits and their own throttling; OTP sends in particular are rate-limited per user. Size it in a real design.

anticipated_questions.q: Does this work for internal users?
anticipated_questions.a: No. Headless Identity is for external identity - Customer and Partner users on a site.
